links.outcome: Readability of consent forms (Fry, SMOG, Flesch-Kincaid for English; GPM, SOL for Spanish)
links.effect: ChatGPT-4.0, English: median Fry 12.0 to 10.0, SMOG 12.3 to 11.7, Flesch-Kincaid 9.2 to 8.6 (all p<0.05). ChatGPT-4.0, Spanish: GPM 9.5 to 10.0, SOL 9.6 to 9.1 (both p>0.05). Custom GPT, English: Fry 12.0 to 7.0, SMOG 12.3 to 9.3, Flesch-Kincaid 9.6 to 5.9 (all p<0.001). Custom GPT, Spanish: SOL 9.5 to 7.3 (p<0.01), GPM unchanged at 8.0 (p>0.99).
links.tradeoff: Spanish gains were absent or modest with direct simplification. Risk disclosure preservation and accuracy were not reported in the abstract.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4.0 modestly improved English readability, with median Fry decreasing from 12.0 to 10.0, SMOG 12.3 to 11.7, and Flesch-Kincaid 9.2 to 8.6 (all p < 0.05).

links.outcome: Readability of Spanish consent forms produced by English-to-Spanish translation targeting a 6th-grade level (GPM, SOL)
links.effect: Custom GPT translation: median GPM 7.0 and SOL 6.8 (both p<0.05 vs original Spanish consents). ChatGPT-4.0 translation: median GPM 8.0 (p=0.25) and SOL 7.6 (p<0.001). For English simplification, the custom GPT's reductions were larger (Fry 12.0 to 7.0) than ChatGPT-4.0's (12.0 to 10.0), but these were tested on different cohorts.
links.tradeoff: Direct Spanish simplification with the custom GPT left GPM unchanged (8.0, p>0.99). The custom GPT was built on ChatGPT-4.0 outputs rather than fine-tuned in the conventional sense.
links.quote: Translation via the custom GPT achieved the largest improvement (median GPM 7.0 and SOL 6.8; both p < 0.05, compared with original Spanish consents).

design_hint: reading-level constrained prompting and translation-based simplification of consent forms
